description: This file implements a Selenium test page object representing the TOTP (one-time password) authenticator setup page within Keycloak's account management console. It extends the base AccountManagement page and overrides the URI builder to append the 'totp' path segment, pointing tests to the correct page location. The class itself contains no additional behavior beyond this URL configuration. It supports UI test automation for verifying two-factor authentication setup flows.

This file provides a small utility class for building standardized OAuth2 error HTTP responses used during client authentication in Keycloak. Its single static method constructs a JAX-RS Response containing an OAuth2ErrorRepresentation with the given status code, error code, and description, formatted as JSON. This centralizes error response creation so that different client authenticator implementations can return consistent, spec-compliant error payloads. It is a lightweight helper class with no state.

This file defines a simple enumeration representing the two possible uses of a cryptographic key in Keycloak: signing (sig) or encryption (enc). Each constant stores the corresponding string value as defined by JOSE/JWK specifications, retrievable through the getSpecName() method. This enum is used throughout Keycloak's cryptography code to distinguish key purpose when generating, storing, or selecting keys for JWT and JWE operations. It has no behavior beyond exposing its associated specification name.

This file implements a JAX-RS container response filter that finalizes the current Keycloak database transaction after a REST request has been processed. It checks whether an active KeycloakTransaction exists in the request context, and commits it if the transaction is healthy or rolls it back if it has been marked rollback-only. This ensures that transactional changes made during request processing are properly persisted or discarded before the response is sent to the client. It is a key piece of Keycloak's request-scoped transaction management.

This file defines a test page object representing a SAML test servlet deployment named 'missing-assertion-sig', used in Keycloak's SAML adapter test suite. It extends a common SAMLServlet base class and injects the deployment's URL via Arquillian resource injection tied to a specific deployment name. The class exposes the injected URL through the getInjectedUrl() method for use by test cases. It supports integration tests that verify SAML assertion signature validation behavior when a signature is missing.

This file implements a cache entity representing a cached list of permission ticket IDs associated with a resource server, used within Keycloak's Infinispan-based authorization cache. It stores the set of permission IDs along with the owning resource server's identifier and a revision number for cache versioning. It implements invalidation logic that marks the cached entry as invalid if either its own ID or its resource server ID appears in a set of invalidated identifiers. This class helps Keycloak efficiently cache and invalidate permission ticket queries for authorization services.

This file defines the core Service Provider Interface (SPI) contract used throughout Keycloak's pluggable provider architecture. It requires implementers to specify whether the SPI is internal, provide a unique name, and declare the associated Provider and ProviderFactory classes. Nearly all of Keycloak's extensible subsystems, such as authentication, storage, and credentials, are built around SPIs implementing this interface. It is a foundational abstraction with no implementation logic of its own.

This file defines the interface for Keycloak's timer service, which is used to schedule recurring background tasks such as session cleanup or periodic synchronization jobs. It declares methods for scheduling a plain Runnable or a more structured ScheduledTask at a given interval, as well as canceling a previously scheduled task by name. A nested TimerTaskContext interface captures the details of a canceled task, allowing it to be restored later if needed. Implementations of this provider back Keycloak's internal scheduled job execution.

This file registers Keycloak's Undertow-based test container integration with the Arquillian test framework. It implements the LoadableExtension interface to register the UndertowAppServer as a deployable container and the UndertowDeploymentArchiveProcessor as an archive processor for test deployments. This allows Keycloak's test suite to run integration and adapter tests against an embedded Undertow server managed by Arquillian. The class contains no logic beyond wiring these two services into the Arquillian extension system.
